texts.label: A
texts.title: Starting at Northfield Gym — your induction

paragraphs.text: Starting at Northfield Gym — your induction. Before using the gym for the first time, every new member must attend a free induction with one of our instructors. Inductions last about 45 minutes and are held every weekday at 7 am, 12 noon and 6 pm, and on Saturdays at 10 am. Book at reception or through the members’ app at least 24 hours in advance; places are limited to four people per session.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: During the induction the instructor will show you how to use the main machines safely, explain how to adjust them to your height and help you plan a simple routine. Please wear trainers and comfortable clothing, and bring a towel and a bottle of water. If you have an injury or a medical condition, tell the instructor at the start.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Once you have completed your induction, your membership card will be activated for the gym floor within 24 hours. Classes such as spinning and yoga do not require an induction but must be booked separately. Members who have used a gym regularly elsewhere in the past six months may ask to skip the induction, but they will need to complete a short questionnaire at reception.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Hospital welcome desk. Greet visitors at the main entrance, give directions and help people who have difficulty walking to find a wheelchair. Shifts are three hours, mornings or afternoons, on any weekday. You will need to complete a half-day training session and a basic background check before starting, which takes about three weeks.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Food bank sorting. Check dates on donated food, sort it into categories and pack parcels for collection. The warehouse is unheated, so warm clothes are essential. Sessions run on Tuesday and Thursday evenings from 6 pm to 8 pm, and you can come as often or as rarely as you like; no training is required.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Reading buddies. Spend an hour a week listening to a primary school pupil read and talking with them about books. You must be available at the same time every week during school term for at least six months, so that the child gets to know you. Training is provided, and a background check is required.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Winter shelter night team. Help set up beds, serve an evening meal and stay overnight at the church hall shelter, which opens from December to March. Volunteers work in pairs and sleep in turns. Each volunteer commits to at least one night a month, and travel costs are refunded.
paragraphs.label: D

texts.label: C
texts.title: Hot desking in the new office

paragraphs.text: Hot desking in the new office. From 1 March, desks on the third and fourth floors will no longer be assigned to individuals. Instead, staff will book a desk for the day using the booking system, which opens two weeks in advance. There are 150 desks for around 220 staff, which is enough because on an average day about a third of employees work from home or are travelling.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Each department has a neighbourhood, an area of the floor where its members are encouraged to book so that teams can sit near each other, but you may book any free desk in the building. If you have not checked in at your desk by 10 am, your booking will be cancelled automatically and the desk released for others. Desks cannot be booked for more than three consecutive days by the same person. Bookings can be made on the system from a phone as well as a computer.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Because desks are shared, nothing may be left on them overnight. Each member of staff has a personal locker in the neighbourhood for laptops, papers and personal items; the key is collected from reception and must be returned if you leave the company. Desks are wiped each evening by the cleaning team, and cleaning wipes are available at the end of every row for use during the day. Food should not be eaten at desks.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Some staff will keep a fixed desk: those whose work requires specialist equipment, and those who need an adjusted workstation for health reasons. To request one, speak to your manager, who will contact the facilities team. Quiet rooms on each floor can be booked for up to two hours for calls or work that needs concentration, and the ground-floor café may be used as informal working space outside lunch hours. The arrangements will be reviewed after six months, and staff will be asked for their views in a short survey.
paragraphs.label: D

texts.label: D
texts.title: Contractors on site: what staff need to know

paragraphs.text: Contractors on site: what staff need to know. Contractors are people who are not employed by the company but carry out work on our premises, such as builders, electricians, cleaners and equipment engineers. Every contractor must sign in at reception on arrival, wear a visitor badge at all times and be escorted by the member of staff who arranged the work, unless they have been given an approved contractor pass. The rules below apply to all of them, whatever the length of the job.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: If you arrange for a contractor to visit, you are the host and are responsible for them while they are on site. Before work begins, you must give them a copy of the site safety rules and show them the fire exits and assembly point. Any work involving heat, such as welding, or work on electrical systems requires a permit issued by the facilities manager at least two working days in advance.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Contractors may use the staff canteen and toilets, but they may not enter server rooms, laboratories or storage areas for chemicals unless the work is in that area and they are accompanied. They must not use company equipment, including ladders and tools, unless this has been agreed in writing beforehand, since the company cannot be sure the equipment is suitable for their work. Contractors’ vehicles may be parked only in the marked bays behind the loading area.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: If you see a contractor working in a way that looks unsafe, you may ask them to stop and must report it to the facilities team immediately; you do not need to be their host to do this. At the end of each day the host checks that the work area has been left safe and that the contractor has signed out. Contractors who break the rules may be asked to leave the site. Any accident or near miss involving a contractor must be recorded in the incident book at reception.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Anyone who drives past a wind farm built twenty years ago and then past one built recently will notice the difference immediately. The newer turbines are far taller, their blades far longer, and there are fewer of them for the same area of land or sea. The growth has been remarkably steady: the typical size of a new turbine has increased several times over since the early 2000s, and the largest machines now stand taller than most skyscrapers. The reasons for this growth lie partly in physics and partly in economics. For people who have followed the industry for a long time, the change is one of the most visible signs of how quickly it has developed, and the contrast is striking even to people with no interest in engineering.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The physics is straightforward. The power a turbine can capture depends on the area swept by its blades, which increases with the square of the blade length: double the length of the blades and the swept area, and therefore the potential power, roughly quadruples. Height matters too, because wind is stronger and steadier further from the ground, where it is less slowed by trees, buildings and uneven terrain. A taller turbine with longer blades therefore produces far more electricity, and produces it more consistently, than a smaller one on the same site. Because wind power rises steeply with wind speed, even a small increase in average speed at greater height produces a considerable gain in output.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The economics reinforce the physics. Many of the costs of a wind farm, such as foundations, cables, roads, planning and maintenance visits, depend more on the number of turbines than on their size. A site with ten large turbines rather than forty small ones needs fewer foundations and fewer connections, and requires fewer technicians to keep it running. The cost of electricity from wind has fallen sharply over the past two decades, and larger turbines are one of the main reasons. Fewer, larger machines also make better use of the limited number of good sites.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Offshore wind has pushed the trend furthest. At sea, winds are stronger and more constant, and there are no neighbours to object to the height or appearance of the machines. The cost of installing each turbine offshore is very high, involving specialised ships and foundations fixed to the seabed or floating in deep water, which makes it especially worthwhile to install fewer, larger units. The biggest turbines built so far have been designed for offshore use, with blades longer than a football pitch. Floating foundations, which are still relatively new, could open up deep waters where fixed foundations are impossible.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Size brings engineering problems of its own. Longer blades are heavier, and their weight increases faster than their length, which places great strain on the hub and the tower. Manufacturers have responded with lighter materials such as carbon fibre, and with blades designed to bend slightly in strong winds rather than resist them rigidly. Transporting the components is another difficulty: blades longer than eighty metres cannot easily be moved by road, which limits where the largest machines can be built on land and favours sites near ports. Some manufacturers have experimented with blades made in sections that are joined on site.
paragraphs.label: E

paragraphs.text: Public attitudes also set limits, particularly on land. In many areas, planning permission for tall turbines is difficult to obtain because of objections about their visual impact, noise and effect on property values. Some countries impose minimum distances between turbines and homes that increase with the height of the turbine, which in practice rules out the largest machines in densely populated regions. Supporters argue that fewer, larger turbines are less intrusive than many small ones, but this view is not shared by everyone living near a proposed site. Offshore sites avoid most of these objections, which is one reason the largest machines have gone to sea.
paragraphs.label: F

paragraphs.text: Not everyone in the industry believes that growth can continue indefinitely. Some engineers argue that the largest offshore turbines are approaching the point at which further increases in size will bring smaller savings, because the costs of the stronger materials, larger ships and heavier foundations required begin to rise faster than the extra output. Others point out that similar predictions have been made before and proved wrong, as new materials and methods allowed designers to overcome limits that had seemed firm. The debate is partly about engineering and partly about how much risk developers are willing to take on untested designs.
paragraphs.label: G

paragraphs.text: For now, the trend towards larger machines shows little sign of slowing, and much of the growth in renewable electricity over the coming decades is expected to come from offshore wind farms built with the biggest turbines available. The history of wind power over the past thirty years is, in large part, the history of a single decision repeated many times: to make each new generation of machines bigger than the last. Whether that decision will continue to make sense is one of the more interesting questions facing the energy industry. The answer will depend as much on ships, ports and planning rules as on the turbines themselves.
paragraphs.label: H

explanation.kk: Көміртек талшығы материал ретінде аталған; үлес пен құрлықтағы турбиналар айтылмаған → NOT GIVEN.

groups.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Text E? Write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

items.quote: double the length of the blades and the swept area, and therefore the potential power, roughly quadruples
items.prompt: a doubling of blade length roughly 36 ____ the possible output

explanation.en: “double the length of the blades and the swept area, and therefore the potential power, roughly quadruples” → quadruples. Not “doubles”: the area grows with the square of the length.
explanation.kk: «double the length of the blades and the swept area, and therefore the potential power, roughly quadruples» → quadruples. «doubles» емес: аудан ұзындықтың квадратымен өседі.
explanation.ru: «double the length of the blades and the swept area, and therefore the potential power, roughly quadruples» → quadruples. Не «doubles»: площадь растёт как квадрат длины.

items.quote: depend more on the number of turbines than on their size
items.prompt: mainly on the 37 ____ of machines

explanation.en: “depend more on the number of turbines than on their size” → number.
explanation.kk: «depend more on the number of turbines than on their size» → number.
explanation.ru: «depend more on the number of turbines than on their size» → number.

items.quote: involving specialised ships and foundations
items.prompt: specialised 38 ____

explanation.en: “involving specialised ships and foundations” → ships.
explanation.kk: «involving specialised ships and foundations» → ships.
explanation.ru: «involving specialised ships and foundations» → ships.

items.quote: cannot easily be moved by road
items.prompt: hard to move by 39 ____

explanation.en: “cannot easily be moved by road” → road. This applies to blades over eighty metres long.
explanation.kk: «cannot easily be moved by road» → road. Ұзындығы 80 метрден асатын қалақтар туралы.
explanation.ru: «cannot easily be moved by road» → road. Речь о лопастях длиннее 80 метров.

items.quote: favours sites near ports
items.prompt: built near 40 ____

explanation.en: “favours sites near ports” → ports. Ports suit them because blades are hard to move by road.
explanation.kk: «favours sites near ports» → ports. Порт ыңғайлы, себебі қалақты жолмен тасу қиын.
explanation.ru: «favours sites near ports» → ports. Порты удобны, потому что лопасти трудно везти по дороге.
